evidence.quote: The panic's hasty retreat should not be confused with robust recovery. For economic performance will turn ultimately on the force of private final demand; and for now, it remains weak.
unemployment rates, in my judgment, are likely to remain higher and linger longer than in recent recessions.

During the transition, there may well be political impetus for still more-aggressive macroeconomic policies. In evaluating new measures, however, policymakers' predominant interest should be ensuring the credibility of their fiscal and monetary frameworks.
The Federal Reserve should not--and will not--compromise another kind of stability--price stability--to help achieve other government policy objectives.
Looking ahead, I could well imagine that the natural rate of unemployment trends higher.

parsed.rationale: The speech describes weak private demand and a likely jobless recovery (dovish on activity) but cautions against more aggressive macro policy, stresses price-stability credibility, and flags a possibly higher NAIRU, giving a slight hawkish tilt. Most of the text concerns structural growth policy rather than the policy rate path, so the net signal is near neutral.
